1.1 ESSENTIAL ELEMENTS OF A CONTRACT, OFFER AND ACCEPTANCE
Introduction
The law relating to contracts in India is contained in INDIAN CONTRACT ACT, 1872. The Act was passed
by British India and is based on the principles of English Common Law. It is applicable to all the states
of India except the state of Jammu and Kashmir. It determines the circumstances

OFFER AND ACCEPTANCE
Offer
The term ‘proposal’ is otherwise called as ‘offer’. An offer is a proposal by one person, whereby he
expresses his willingness to enter into a contractual obligation in return for promise, act or forbearance.

Section 233 provides that in cases where the agent is personally liable, a person dealing with him may
hold either him or his principal, or both of them liable.
Example – A enters into a contract with B to sell him 100 bales of cotton and afterwards discovers that
B was acting as agent for C. A may sue either B or C, or both, for the price of the cotton.

Unpaid seller

• when a bill of exchange or other negotiable instrument has been received as conditional payment,

Sale of Goods Act, 1930

4. Suit for interest: [Sec. 61]
Where there is specific agreement between the seller and the buyer regarding interest on the price
of goods, the seller may claim it from the date when payment becomes due. If there is no specific
agreement, the interest is payable from the date notified by the seller to the buyer.

MATERIAL ALTERATION
Any material alteration of a negotiable instrument renders the same void as against anyone who is a
party thereto at the time of making such alteration and does not consent thereto, unless it was made
in order to carry out the common intention of the original parties:

3.3 ACCEPTANCE, ASSIGNMENT AND NEGOTIATION
ACCEPTANCE
Only certain types of bills require acceptance. Essentials of a valid acceptance are—
(i) Must be written on the face of the bill,
(ii) The bill must be signed by drawee or his authorized agent.
(iii) The accepted bill is required to be delivered to the holder of the instrument.

transferred to any person, so as to constitute that person the holder thereof, the instrument is said to
be negotiated.

designated partner, every partner shall be a designated partner;
• Any partner may become or cease to be a designated part

14.1 ETHICS – Meaning, Importance, Nature and Relevances to Business
Ethics
Ethics is a set of rules that define right and wrong conduct. The term ‘ethics’ derived from Latin word
‘ethos’ which means character. Ethics is a social science which deals with concepts such as right and
wrong, moral and immoral, good and bad behavior of dealing with one another.
